name: Frigate NVR
param_style: peewee 4.5 (SqliteDatabase): ? positional, IN lists expanded, JSONField paths bound as parameters, % compiles to GLOB
schema_source: migrations/001-040 applied in order (raw-SQL DDL copied; peewee migrator steps rendered with peewee's SQLite column types), cross-checked against frigate/models.py
data_scale: scale 1: 10 cameras, ~170k 10-second recording segments (24 h continuous on every camera plus 30 days of motion bursts and one expired day; busy cameras 2-2.5x the quiet ones; a sub stream on one camera), 30k events with JSON data (plus 400 from a removed camera), 91k timeline rows, 12k review segments, 15.6k user review statuses, 7.2k previews; about 150 MB. frigate#24043's reporter had 42 cameras with 283k events, 695k recordings, 972k timeline rows and 120k review segments
visibility_note: 37k stars; the most popular open-source NVR, a Home Assistant staple; SQLite is its only database
interest_note: Time-ordered list and summary endpoints over large, append-only tables whose indexes don't match the ORDER BY: review list/summary with LEFT JOIN review status and per-local-day CASE sums grouped by CAST(start_time + tz) / 86400, timeline ordered by an unindexed timestamp, previews with a 3-way OR range test, JSON GLOB label filters, an events summary grouped by the JSON payload, retention scans and big IN-list deletes.
reach_note: widely self-hosted (Docker, Home Assistant add-on); SQLite is the only backend

cpu_evidence.summary: 42 cameras, 283k events / 695k recordings / 972k timeline / 120k review rows (1.8 GB): event count 0.9 s, timeline count 2.3 s, recording count 6.9 s, review list for 24 h and daily review summary >12 s, latest timeline rows >12 s, one-camera events 8.3-8.7 s, previews for 24 h 1.5 s; proposed indexes not merged (only event camera,start_time landed as migration 039)
misc backend performance work on the review/explore handlers: replaced per-id lookup loops with single IN queries and narrowed the explore column list; added event (camera, start_time) index
UI slow on systems with 150+ cameras; every list endpoint carries the allowed-camera IN list, which grows with the camera count
